items.abstract: Among the top ten most critical security threats to online applications, injection attacks have consistently ranked third according to the Open Web Application Security Project (OWASP), a ranking that has held since 2021. Injection attacks include cross-site scripting (XSS), SQL injection (SQLi), and command injection, and cybercriminals continue to develop more sophisticated methods for carrying them out. This research uses large language models (LLMs) to detect XSS, SQLi, and command injection threats, fine-tuning meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B, distilbert-base-uncased, openai-community/gpt2, and openai-community/gpt2-medium to classify web application payloads as either malicious or benign. LLaMA-3.2-1B achieved the strongest overall performance, with 99.80\% accuracy and recall, 99.82\% precision, and 99.81\% F1-score. DistilBERT-base-uncased achieved comparably strong results (accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score all at 99.80\%), despite having only 0.93\% of its 67.6 million parameters (630,532) trainable. TheGPT-2 and GPT-2-medium models achieved slightly lower but still strong performance, at approximately 99.7--99.8\% accuracy and precision. These results demonstrate that fine-tuned LLMs, including comparatively parameter-efficient models such as DistilBERT, can achieve near-perfect accuracy in classifying injection-attack payloads, with LLaMA-3.2-1B showing the strongest overall performance and generalization across the dataset.
title: Utilizing Large Language Model Algorithm for XSS, SQL, and Command Injection Detection

items.abstract: <jats:p>Current benchmarks for evaluating graph reasoning in Large Language Models (LLMs) predominantly utilize pre-constructed, idealized graphs, thereby omitting the structural complexity inherent in enterprise environments. To bridge this gap, we introduce EntKGBench (Enterprise Knowledge Graph Benchmark), an evaluation framework constructed from authentic enterprise records spanning Basic Graph Queries to Complex Algorithms to assess query-conditioned graph construction and multi-step reasoning. Our empirical analysis reveals a ``Cold Start&apos;&apos; Penalty: while frontier models perform adequately in zero-shot semantic retrieval, their performance drops significantly when required to extract relevant topological structures from noisy data to execute systematic algorithmic reasoning. Finally, we identify an ``Alignment Tax&apos;&apos; in Reinforcement Learning (RL) applied to graph reasoning: while outcome-based RL enhances target-driven local search, it concurrently degrades stability in sequential reasoning tasks reliant on global context.</jats:p>
title: EntKGBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Model Reasoning on Real-World Enterprise Knowledge Graphs

items.abstract: <jats:p>This paper introduces the Token Pagination Framework (TPF), a formal protocol for managing context window resources in enterprise Large Language Model (LLM) deployments. Context overflow-the condition in which session token budgets are exhausted before a task completes-is a pervasive, expensive, and undertheorized problem in production AI systems. The problem is structurally compounded by the Model Context Protocol (MCP), which introduces two distinct token inflation vectors into every agentic session: upfront tool schema loading and accumulating tool result payloads. Existing work addresses token budgeting within single model invocations or at prompt construction time, but no prior framework treats the context window as a paginated resource with a persistent cursor, layered admission gates, and a structured overflow signal. TPF borrows the REST API pagination contract and maps it rigorously onto LLM session management. We define six quantitative metrics: Context Pressure Index (CPI), Semantic Density Score (SDS), Recency Decay Weight (RDW), Intent Coverage Ratio (ICR), Output Verbosity Ratio (OVR), and Tool Schema Pressure (TSP). We derive a unified admission predicate, a rolling compression operator, and a cursor state model extended for MCP tool state. The architecture is organized as four layers: Gate, Budget, Compression, and Overflow. TPF maps directly onto the MCP host role defined in the Model Context Protocol specification and is designed to inform protocol-level features in AI provider APIs, MCP host implementations, and orchestration runtimes.</jats:p>
title: Token Pagination: A Formal Framework for Context-bounded Inference in Enterprise Large Language Model Systems

items.abstract: <jats:p>Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has emerged as an effective paradigm for grounding Large Language Models (LLMs) with external knowledge, thereby reducing hallucinations and improving factual consistency in document-centric question answering. However, most practical RAG deployments rely on cloud-hosted Application Programming Interfaces (APIs), remote vector stores, or proprietary inference services, raising privacy, sovereignty, latency, and cost concerns for government, defense, finance, healthcare, and industrial organizations. This paper presents a fully local offline RAG framework that transforms Portable Document Format (PDF) rulebooks and enterprise documents into a secure on-premise conversational intelligence system without requiring external APIs or cloud connectivity.The proposed framework integrates page-wise PDF ingestion using PyMuPDF, document normalization, metadata-aware semantic chunking, local embedding generation using nomic-embed-text, Chroma vector database indexing, and answer synthesis through Ollama-hosted LLMs, including the Meta Llama 3 8-billion-parameter model and the Qwen 2.5 14-billion-parameter model. Structured metadata extraction, source-grounded citation generation, low-memory model routing, and an interactive Streamlit interface further support practical deployment. A hybrid retrieval strategy combining dense semantic similarity with metadata constraints is introduced to improve retrieval precision for rule-based documents.A real-world case study using the General Financial Rules (GFR 2017) demonstrates the effectiveness of the framework for procurement and compliance question answering. Experimental results show competitive retrieval quality, low hallucination rates, acceptable response latency, and modest memory requirements on consumer-grade hardware while preserving data confidentiality and eliminating recurring API costs. The proposed framework provides a practical approach for privacy-preserving enterprise document intelligence and sovereign Artificial Intelligence (AI) deployment.</jats:p>
title: A Fully Local Offline Framework for Enterprise Document Intelligence Using Retrieval-Based Large Language Model Grounding

items.abstract: <jats:p>The enterprise deployment of artificial intelligence language models presents organizations with critical architectural decisions between Small Language Models and Large Language Models, each offering distinct advantages and operational considerations. Small Language Models, characterized by parameter counts ranging from millions to several billion, provide computational efficiency, rapid deployment capabilities, and cost-effective solutions for real-time applications requiring millisecond response times. Large Language Models, featuring billions to trillions of parameters, deliver sophisticated contextual understanding, complex reasoning abilities, and comprehensive knowledge bases suitable for advanced content generation and analytical tasks. Enterprise environments must evaluate infrastructure requirements, with Small Language Models operating effectively on standard CPU configurations and minimal memory footprints, while Large Language Models demand GPU clusters and substantial computational resources. The architectural choice significantly impacts system performance, operational costs, scalability potential, and long-term strategic positioning. Contemporary enterprise implementations increasingly recognize hybrid deployment strategies that leverage the complementary strengths of both model categories, enabling organizations to optimize resource utilization while addressing diverse application requirements. Future developments in neural architecture search, hardware-software co-design methodologies, and federated learning frameworks promise to reshape enterprise AI deployment strategies, creating opportunities for more efficient and scalable artificial intelligence solutions.</jats:p>
title: Choosing the Right Model for Enterprise AI Applications: A Comprehensive Analysis of Small Language Models versus Large Language Models in Enterprise Architecture
